Hi Evan / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clarity on SyncWave's production timeline and the desire to lock-in unit economics for the next 3 years. Per our conversation I've attached a concise term sheet and a draft SOW for the proposed commitment. High-level offer: a 3-year agreement with a laddered prepay that balances price and cashflow:

- Committed ARR: $1,500,000/year (metered usage against committed units)
- Term discount: 18% off list for a 3-year committed term
- Payment profile (proposed): 30% upfront at signing, then remaining balance invoiced quarterly against milestones (usage reconciliation).
- Standard invoicing: Net 60.

We know large enterprises often request extended payment terms. We can consider a finance exception (Net 90) on the remaining invoiced balance only if SyncWave is willing to:

1) Execute the 3-year commitment (non-cancelable for committed units), and
2) Put the upfront portion (30%) into an escrow arrangement or provide an irrevocable bank guarantee/PO that meets our finance criteria.

Attachments: Redwood_TermSheet_SyncWave_v3.pdf, SOW-Draft-SyncWave.docx

Next steps: If that framework looks reasonable, Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate the contract path and Ben can work with your procurement on acceptable escrow/PO language. Would you be able to confirm by EOD Thursday (7/23) so we can reserve the capacity window for September?

Best,

Tessa — thanks for the clear proposal and attachments. A few items from procurement we need addressed before taking this to legal:

- Payment term: SyncWave standard is Net 90 for enterprise agreements. Our treasury team needs the full 90 days on invoice.
- Upfront: we can accept 25% upfront (not 30%) if Redwood will reduce the upfront cash requirement in favor of a signed 3-year PO.
- Escrow: procurement is open to an escrow mechanism, but it must be run by our counsel (we'll share a template).
- SOC2 / security: procurement needs an evidence packet (SOC2 Type II, data residency notes) before we sign.

Could you provide a version of the term sheet with Net 90 as the default and a 25% upfront option? Also, we'll need an explicit milestone schedule in the SOW that ties quarterly billing to delivery/enablement checkpoints.

On schedule: if we can get final commercial terms by next Friday (7/31), legal has bandwidth to review in the first week of August.

Appreciate it — Evan

Marissa / Tessa — saw Evan's ask for Net 90 and 25% upfront. Flags for finance/legal:

- Net 90 on all invoices is a meaningful working-capital risk. We should avoid agreeing to Net 90 on the entire cashflow unless there's mitigation (escrow/LC/PO/advanced partial payment).
- Proposed compromise (internal): 30% upfront (we can consider 25% if they provide an irrevocable PO + escrow deposit equivalent to 10% of year one), remaining invoiced quarterly with Net 60.
- If procurement insists on Net 90 only, we can grant Net 90 on the remaining invoiced balance (not the upfront) provided SyncWave: (a) executes a 3-year non-cancelable commitment for committed units; (b) agrees to an escrow or bank guarantee for the upfront; and (c) provides SOC2 evidence before go-live.

Action items:
- Marissa: can you draft a redline to the term sheet with two columns: (A) Standard offer (30% upfront, Net 60); (B) Procurement path (25% upfront + PO/escrow, Net 90 on remaining balance). Also add an optional clause for an irrevocable LC if they prefer that to escrow.
- Tessa: loop in legal on procurement's escrow template and send SOC2 evidence pack (we have the latest SOC2 report in Drive).

I'll mark this high priority — SyncWave is large ARR potential.
